title: CACHING
subtitle: Keep hot data in memory so most reads never reach the database.
footer: System Design, Step by Step · core concepts

items: On a miss, read the database.
Populate the cache with a TTL.
The next request is served from memory.
On writes, update the DB and delete (not update) the cached key, so the next read refreshes it.

head: Strategy
Trade-off
rows: Default; app controls; possible brief staleness
Write cache + DB together; fresher, slower writes
Write cache, flush later; fast, risk of loss
Edge cache for static or shared responses

items: Add a cache when numbers show the DB can't keep up, or a read path misses its latency target.
Default: cache-aside. Read cache → on miss read DB → set with TTL.
On write: update the DB, then DELETE the key (safe under concurrent writers).
Always set a TTL so invalidation bugs heal themselves.
Guard hot keys: single-flight rebuilds, jittered TTLs, local L1 cache.
Never cache what must be exact at checkout.

blocks.text: "Reads outnumber writes 100 to 1 and popularity is skewed, so cache-aside Redis should absorb 80–90% of reads."
